extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners working on automated evaluation of LLM-generated creative writing (NLP/ML researchers, computational creativity specialists)
extracted.subtask_description: Automated, reference-based evaluation of creative short-story outputs from large language models using the Torrance Test of Creative Writing (TTCW) with Likert-style, pairwise comparisons to human-authored reference stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fluency — Does the end of the story feel natural and earned, as opposed to arbitrary or abrupt?
rubrics_metrics.description: A TTCW fluency test question asking whether the story's ending feels earned rather than abrupt or arbitrary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the TTCW fluency dimension (one of 14 binary tests). In the proposed framework this is evaluated comparatively against a human reference using a 5-point Likert (significantly better +2 to significantly worse -2), with order alternated and each test conducted twice; pass/fail determined by average vs cutoff (see Reference-based Likert-style comparison and Binary score conversion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fluency — Do the different elements of the story work together to form a unified, engaging, and satisfying whole?
rubrics_metrics.description: A TTCW fluency test question assessing overall unity and engagement of story elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated as a binary TTCW test via reference-based comparative Likert scoring; aggregated across trials and converted to pass/fail per the framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fluency — Does the story have an appropriate balance between scene and summary/exposition, or does it rely too heavily on one element?
rubrics_metrics.description: TTCW fluency question about balance of scene vs summary/exposition in narrative pacing and presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed relative to reference text using the proposed Likert-based comparison and binary conversion procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fluency — Does the manipulation of time (compression or stretching) feel appropriate and balanced?
rubrics_metrics.description: TTCW fluency question about temporal manipulation and whether it reads as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of fluency tests assessed via the reference-based approach; consider coherence of temporal shifts relative to the reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fluency — Does the story make sophisticated use of idiom, metaphor, or literary allusion?
rubrics_metrics.description: TTCW fluency question probing use of figurative language and literary allusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated comparatively; sophisticated, contextually appropriate use should score better than reference; assessed via Likert and binary thresholding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility — Does the story achieve a good balance between interiority and exteriority, in a way that feels emotionally flexible?
rubrics_metrics.description: TTCW flexibility question on balance between internal perspective (interiority) and external action/description (exteriority).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judged relative to the reference; surprising-but-appropriate turns and balanced emotional perspective are indicators of higher flexibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility — Does the story contain turns that are both surprising and appropriate?
rubrics_metrics.description: TTCW flexibility question assessing whether plot/idea turns are unexpected yet fitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originality of turns that remain grounded in the story's logic is rewarded; comparative Likert ratings capture relative surprise/appropriateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility — Does the story provide diverse perspectives, and if there are unlikeable characters, are their perspectives presented convincingly and accurately?
rubrics_metrics.description: TTCW flexibility question on diversity of perspectives and credible portrayal of unlikeable characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess convincingness and variety of viewpoint representation compared to reference; included in the 14 binary TTCW tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality — Is the story an original piece of writing without any clichés?
rubrics_metrics.description: TTCW originality question checking for absence of clichés and overall originality of content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original, non-clichéd expressions score better; evaluated comparatively against reference using Likert then converted to binary pass/fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality — Does the story show originality in its form and/or structure?
rubrics_metrics.description: TTCW originality question about formal/structural innovation or novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether structure/form differ from conventional patterns in a meaningful way; judged relative to the reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality — Will an average reader of this story obtain a unique and original idea from reading it?
rubrics_metrics.description: TTCW originality question probing whether the story conveys a new or distinct idea to a typical reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured comparatively; rewards texts that deliver unique conceptual content or insights relative to the reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elaboration — Are there passages in the story that involve subtext, and if so, does the subtext enrich the setting or feel forced?
rubrics_metrics.description: TTCW elaboration question evaluating presence and quality of subtext and whether it enriches rather than feels contrived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare the subtlety and contribution of subtext to the reference; strong, organic subtext is favorable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elaboration — Does the writer make the fictional world believable at the sensory level?
rubrics_metrics.description: TTCW elaboration question concerning sensory detail and world-building believability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess sensory richness and plausibility of the fictional setting relative to the reference; part of binary pass/fail TTCW tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elaboration — Does each character feel developed with appropriate complexity, ensuring no character exists solely for plot convenience?
rubrics_metrics.description: TTCW elaboration question checking character development and avoidance of purely plot-convenient characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate depth and believable motivations of characters compared to reference; contributes to the TTCW binary score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference-based Likert-style comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Core methodological rubric: compare each candidate story directly to a high-quality human reference story using a 5-level Likert comparison: 'significantly better' (+2), 'slightly better' (+1), 'the same' (0), 'slightly worse' (-1), 'significantly worse' (-2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To reduce positional bias, alternate the order of candidate and reference and perform each test twice. For each TTCW test, compute the average of the two ratings; convert to a binary pass/fail using a cutoff threshold and sum passes across the 14 tests to produce an overall creativity score (0–14). This reference-based relative scoring is central to improved alignment with human judgments in the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order alternation and repeat trials to reduce positional bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational requirement: alternate the sequence of candidate and reference (candidate-first vs reference-first) and conduct each test twice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Averaging over two oppositely-ordered trials minimizes positional/bias effects in comparative judgments before binary conversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Binary score conversion and cutoff selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Convert averaged Likert comparison scores for each test into binary pass/fail labels using a cutoff score; the paper finds an optimal cutoff at -2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binary conversion aligns TTCW's binary test nature with automated scoring and improved interpretability. The authors empirically tuned the cutoff (hyperparameter search) and report best ranking similarity with cutoff = -2 (interpreted as allowing candidates slightly worse than reference to still pass).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompting strategy — Analyze-Rate (zero-shot CoT style)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of directly asking the model to output a rating, prompt it to first analyze the sample according to evaluation criteria and then provide a final score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This analyze-then-rate strategy (similar to zero-shot Chain-of-Thought) improves LLM evaluator performance and stability; ablation shows removing it reduces ranking similarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Likert scale granularity recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Choice of rating granularity influences alignment: the paper compares 3-, 5-, and 7-point Likert scales and recommends a 5-point scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical results showed 5-point outperformed 3-point and 7-point for Spearman correlation in their experiments; use 5-point when following this framework unless revalidated on new data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate scoring: total number of TTCW tests passed (0–14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall creativity score for a candidate story is the count of TTCW tests (out of 14) that the candidate passes after binary conversion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this aggregate to rank candidate stories for the same prompt/storyline; rankings are then compared to human expert rankings with standard rank-correlation metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation metrics for alignment with human judgments
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Spearman's rank correlation, Kendall's tau, and pairwise accuracy to quantify how well automated evaluator rankings match human expert rankings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pairwise accuracy is reported prominently (proportion of correctly aligned pairwise comparisons). Authors present AVG Spearman, AVG Kendall’s Tau and pairwise accuracy across models and use these metrics to compare baseline and proposed methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ablation and component importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Test the contribution of individual components (Reference-Based Approach and Analyze-Rate Strategy) via ablation to verify their importance for evaluation performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper shows both components independently improve performance; removing either reduces ranking similarity and evaluation stability, so include both in implementations if possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robustness & generalization testing (cross-dataset/reference setup)
rubrics_metrics.description: Validate the framework on datasets with different rating scales and reference availability (e.g., datasets using 10-point scales or using GPT-4 generated references rather than human texts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The method should be tested for generalization; the paper demonstrates reasonable alignment even when adapting to datasets with different settings, but recommends careful handling when references are non-human or when all candidates are far inferior to the reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations & risk mitigation: reference reliance and bias amplification
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledged limitation that reliance on reference stories can reduce scalability and potentially amplify stylistic/cultural biases present in the chosen references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mitigate risks by careful selection of diverse references and maintaining some level of human oversight; be cautious when all candidates are much worse than references as comparative labels may collapse (all 'significantly worse').
